title: In the beginning
text: Before there was anything at all, before the sun, before the sea, before even one small stone, there was God.
And God spoke. “Let there be light,” God said, and there was light, bright and warm and new. God looked at the light, and it was good.

Then God made the sky, high and wide, and gathered the waters into seas, so that dry land appeared. On the land God made grass and trees and flowers, each with seeds inside, ready to grow. God made the sun for the day, and the moon and the stars for the night.
God filled the sea with fish and the sky with birds. God made cows and sheep, foxes and beetles, and every creature that creeps and scurries and runs. And God looked at all of it, and it was good.
Last of all, God made people: a man and a woman, made in God's own image, to love God and to look after the world, as a gardener looks after a garden.
God looked at everything that had been made, and it was very good. And on the seventh day God rested, and blessed that day, and made it holy: a day for rest, and for delight.
wonder: I wonder what you would have liked to watch God make.
I wonder what in our world you think is very good.
I wonder how we can look after the world God made.
prayer: Thank you, God, for making the light and the stars, the animals and me. Help me look after your world. Amen.

title: Noah and the rainbow
text: A long time ago, the world had grown full of cruelty, and God was sad. But there was one man, Noah, who still walked with God.
God told Noah, “Make a great boat, an ark, out of wood, and make it watertight. Bring your family into it, and two of every kind of living creature, to keep them alive.”
So Noah built the ark, just as God told him. Then in they came: lions and lambs, elephants and mice, two by two. Noah and his family went in, and God shut the door.
The rain fell and fell, for forty days and forty nights, until the water covered even the hills. But the ark floated safely on the water, and everyone inside was kept safe.
At last the rain stopped. Noah sent out a dove, and it came back with a fresh olive leaf in its beak. The land was drying! Soon the ark came to rest, and the animals stepped out into the sunshine.

Then God put a rainbow in the clouds. “This is my promise,” said God, “to you and to every living creature: never again will a flood destroy the earth. Whenever you see the rainbow, I will remember my promise.”
wonder: I wonder what it sounded like inside the ark.
I wonder how Noah felt when the dove came back with a leaf.
I wonder what you think of when you see a rainbow.
prayer: Thank you, God, that you keep your promises. When I see a rainbow, help me remember you. Amen.

title: Rebecca at the well
text: Abraham was very old, and he wanted a good wife for his son Isaac. So he sent his oldest servant on a long journey, with ten camels, back to the land of Abraham's family.

In the evening the servant reached a well outside a town, where the women came to draw water. He was tired and far from home, and he prayed: “Lord, show your kindness. Let the young woman who says, ‘Drink, and I'll water your camels too,’ be the one you have chosen.”
Before he had even finished praying, a young woman called Rebecca came out with a jar on her shoulder. She filled it at the spring.
“Please may I have a little water?” the servant asked. “Drink,” said Rebecca, and she lowered her jar. Then she said, “I'll draw water for your camels too, until they have finished drinking.”
Ten thirsty camels drink a great deal of water! Rebecca ran back and forth to the well again and again, until every camel had had enough.
The servant bowed his head and thanked God, who had led him to the right place. Rebecca's family welcomed him, and Rebecca chose to go with him, to marry Isaac. And Isaac loved her.
wonder: I wonder why Rebecca was so kind to a stranger.
I wonder how tired her arms were after all those camels.
I wonder who you could be kind to tomorrow, even if they don't ask.
prayer: Dear God, thank you for kind people. Help me to do more than I'm asked, with a happy heart. Amen.

title: The baby in the basket
text: Long ago in Egypt, God's people, the Israelites, were made to work as slaves. The king, called Pharaoh, was afraid of them, and he gave a terrible order: every baby boy born to them must be thrown into the river.

One mother had a beautiful baby boy, and she hid him for three months. When she couldn't hide him any longer, she made a little basket out of reeds, covered it with tar so it wouldn't leak, and laid her baby in it. She put the basket among the tall reeds at the edge of the river Nile.
His big sister, Miriam, stood a little way off to watch.
Then Pharaoh's daughter, the princess, came down to the river to bathe. She saw the basket and sent her maid to fetch it. When she opened it, the baby was crying, and she felt sorry for him.
Miriam ran up. “Shall I go and find a woman to nurse the baby for you?” “Yes, go,” said the princess. And Miriam ran and fetched… the baby's own mother!
So the baby was safe, and his mother looked after him until he was older. Then he went to live with the princess, who named him Moses. One day God would use Moses to set his people free.
wonder: I wonder how Miriam felt, watching from the reeds.
I wonder what the mother whispered as she let the basket go.
I wonder who watches over you.
prayer: Thank you, God, for watching over babies and children, and over me. Make me brave like Miriam. Amen.

title: Water from the rock
text: God had set his people free from Egypt, and Moses was leading them through the wilderness towards a new home. The wilderness was hot and dry and stony.

One day they camped in a place where there was no water at all. The children were thirsty, the animals were thirsty, and everyone was cross. “Give us water!” they grumbled at Moses. “Why did you bring us out here?”
Moses cried out to God: “What shall I do with these people?”

God said, “Take your staff, the stick you carry, and walk on ahead with some of the elders. I will be standing there before you on the rock. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it, so that the people can drink.”
So Moses did exactly that, while the elders watched. He struck the rock, and out came water: cool, clear water, splashing and running, enough for everyone and every animal.

The people drank and drank. Moses called that place Massah and Meribah, which means “testing” and “arguing”, because the people had asked, “Is the Lord among us or not?” And God had answered: yes, I am.
wonder: I wonder what the first splash of water sounded like.
I wonder why the people grumbled instead of asking.
I wonder when you have felt that God was with you.
prayer: Thank you, God, for water to drink and food to eat. When I'm cross, help me ask you instead of grumbling. Amen.

title: The shepherd boy and the giant
text: David was the youngest of eight brothers, and his job was to look after his father's sheep in the hills near Bethlehem. Out there, he learned to be brave: when a lion or a bear took a lamb, David went after it and rescued the lamb.

One day there was a war. The army of the Philistines stood on one hill, and the army of Israel on another, with a valley in between. Every day a giant called Goliath stepped out and shouted, “Send me a man to fight!” He was enormously tall, with a bronze helmet and a huge spear. Everyone was terrified.
David came to bring food to his brothers, and he heard the giant. “Who is he,” said David, “to defy the armies of the living God? I'll go.”

King Saul gave David his own armour, but it was far too big and heavy. David took it off. Instead, he took his shepherd's staff, chose five smooth stones from the stream, and walked out with his sling.

Goliath laughed at him. But David said, “You come to me with a sword and a spear, but I come to you in the name of the Lord.” He put a stone in his sling, whirled it round, and let it fly. The stone struck Goliath on the forehead, and the giant fell down flat on his face.
The shepherd boy had won, not because he was big, but because he trusted God. Many years later, David became king.
wonder: I wonder what giants feel big and scary to you.
I wonder why David took off the king's armour.
I wonder what it means to trust God when you are small.
prayer: Dear God, when something feels too big for me, help me remember that you are with me. Amen.

title: Elijah and the ravens
text: Elijah was a prophet, someone who listened to God and passed on God's message. In his time, the king of Israel was Ahab, who had turned away from God.
Elijah went to King Ahab and said, “As the Lord lives, there will be no dew and no rain in these years, until I say so.” And the rain stopped.
Then God told Elijah, “Go away and hide by the brook Cherith, east of the Jordan. You can drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”

So Elijah went and lived by the little brook. Every morning, big black ravens came flapping down with bread and meat in their beaks. And every evening they came again, with bread and meat. Elijah drank from the brook, and he was never hungry.
Ravens don't usually share their food with anyone! But God can look after us in the most surprising ways.
Elijah stayed there, alone but not forgotten, waiting quietly for what God would ask him to do next.
wonder: I wonder what Elijah thought the first time a raven landed beside him.
I wonder how it feels to wait and not know what's next.
I wonder who God sends to look after you.
prayer: Thank you, God, for the people who look after me every day. Help me trust you when I have to wait. Amen.

title: The jar that never ran out
text: There was still no rain, and the brook where Elijah lived dried up. So God said, “Go to the town of Zarephath. I have told a widow there to feed you.”
At the town gate, Elijah saw a woman gathering sticks. “Please could you bring me a little water,” he said, “and a piece of bread?”

The woman turned to him, very sad. “I have no bread,” she said. “I have only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. I'm gathering sticks to make one last meal for my son and me. After that we will have nothing left.”

“Don't be afraid,” said Elijah. “Go and make your meal, but first make a little loaf for me. For God says: the jar of flour will not run out, and the jug of oil will not run dry, until the day the Lord sends rain.”
It was a hard thing to share when she had so little. But she went and did as Elijah said.

And every day, when she reached into the jar, there was flour. Every day, when she tipped the jug, there was oil. The woman, her son and Elijah had enough to eat for many days, just as God had promised.
wonder: I wonder how brave the woman had to be to share her last flour.
I wonder what her son said when the jar was full again.
I wonder what we could share, even when we don't have much.
prayer: Dear God, thank you that there is always enough with you. Help us share what we have. Amen.

title: Jonah and the great fish
text: God said to Jonah, “Go to the great city of Nineveh and tell them to stop doing wicked things.” But Jonah didn't want to go. He ran the other way, and got on a ship sailing far across the sea.

Then God sent a great wind. The waves rose like mountains, the ship creaked and tipped, and the sailors were so frightened that they threw the cargo overboard. And where was Jonah? Fast asleep below deck!
The captain woke him. “How can you sleep? Get up and pray!” Jonah told them, “This storm is my fault. I am running away from God. Throw me into the sea and it will be calm.”

The sailors didn't want to, but at last they did, and the sea grew still. And God sent a great fish to swallow Jonah up. Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights, and there, in the dark, he prayed.
Then God spoke to the fish, and it spat Jonah out onto dry land.
God said a second time, “Go to Nineveh.” And this time Jonah went. The people of Nineveh listened, and turned away from their wicked ways. And God, who is kind and slow to anger, forgave them.
wonder: I wonder why Jonah ran away.
I wonder what it was like to pray inside a fish.
I wonder what it feels like to get a second chance.
prayer: Dear God, thank you for second chances. When I want to run away from what is right, turn me round. Amen.

title: The angel's news
text: In a small town called Nazareth there lived a young woman named Mary. She was engaged to marry a carpenter called Joseph.
One day God sent the angel Gabriel to her. “Rejoice, you who are highly favoured!” said the angel. “The Lord is with you.”
Mary was very puzzled, and a little afraid. What could this mean?

“Don't be afraid, Mary,” said Gabriel. “God is pleased with you. You will have a baby boy, and you will name him Jesus. He will be great, and he will be called the Son of the Most High, and his kingdom will never end.”
“How can this be?” asked Mary. Gabriel told her that the Holy Spirit would come upon her, so the child would be holy, the Son of God. “Nothing is impossible with God.”
Mary was quiet for a moment. Then she said, “I am the Lord's servant. Let it be to me as you have said.” And the angel left her.
wonder: I wonder what an angel's voice sounds like.
I wonder how Mary found the courage to say yes.
I wonder what God might be asking you to say yes to.
prayer: Dear God, help me to say yes to you, like Mary did. Nothing is impossible with you. Amen.

title: The shepherds on the hill
text: Mary and Joseph had to travel to Bethlehem, Joseph's family town, to be counted by the Romans. When they arrived, the town was full, and there was no room for them in the guest room.
While they were there, Mary's baby was born. She wrapped him in strips of cloth and laid him in a manger, the box the animals eat from.
Out in the fields nearby, shepherds were looking after their sheep in the dark. Suddenly an angel stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone all around. They were terrified!

“Don't be afraid,” said the angel. “I bring you good news of great joy for all people. Today a Saviour has been born for you in the city of David: Christ the Lord. You will find him wrapped in cloths, lying in a manger.”
Then the whole sky was filled with angels, praising God: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, goodwill towards people!”

When the angels had gone, the shepherds said, “Let's go and see!” They hurried to Bethlehem and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger, just as they had been told. They went home glorifying God, and Mary kept all these things in her heart.
wonder: I wonder why the news came to shepherds first.
I wonder what the sky full of angels looked like.
I wonder what you would bring to the baby Jesus.
prayer: Thank you, God, for sending Jesus to be born for us, in a little stable. Glory to you! Amen.

title: The wise men and the star
text: Far away in the East, some wise men studied the stars. One night they saw a new star rising, and they knew it meant that a great king had been born. So they packed up and set out on a long journey to find him.
They came to Jerusalem and asked, “Where is the one who has been born King of the Jews? We saw his star and have come to worship him.”

King Herod heard this and was worried: he didn't want another king! He found out from the priests that the Messiah was to be born in Bethlehem. “Go and search for the child,” Herod told the wise men, “and tell me when you find him.”
The wise men went on, and the star went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was. When they saw it, they were filled with joy.
They went into the house and saw the child with his mother, Mary. They knelt down and worshipped him, and opened their treasures: gold, frankincense and myrrh.
That night God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod. So they went home another way.
wonder: I wonder how long the wise men travelled.
I wonder why they were so full of joy when the star stopped.
I wonder what gift you could give to Jesus.
prayer: Dear God, like the wise men, help me follow you and bring you my best. Amen.

title: The journey by night
text: After the wise men had gone, an angel came to Joseph in a dream. “Get up!” said the angel. “Take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt. Herod is going to search for the child to hurt him. Stay there until I tell you.”
Joseph didn't wait until morning. He got up at once, in the dark, and took Mary and little Jesus, and they set off on the long road to Egypt.
It was a hard journey, far from home. But they were together, and God was watching over them.
They stayed in Egypt, a foreign land, as strangers. Long, long before, God's people had lived in Egypt too, and God had brought them out. Now God would bring Jesus out again.
When Herod died, the angel came to Joseph in another dream. “Get up, take the child and his mother, and go back home. The ones who wanted to hurt him are gone.”
So Joseph took his family home, and they settled in the little town of Nazareth. And there Jesus grew up.
wonder: I wonder how Mary felt, packing up in the middle of the night.
I wonder what it is like to be a stranger in a new country.
I wonder how we could welcome a family who is far from home.
prayer: Dear God, keep safe every family who has had to leave home. Help us to welcome strangers. Amen.

title: Jesus is baptised
text: Jesus grew up in Nazareth. When he was about thirty years old, he went down to the river Jordan, where his cousin John was baptising people.
John was calling people to turn back to God. Crowds came to him, and he dipped them in the river as a sign that they were washed clean and starting again.
When Jesus came to be baptised, John was surprised. “I need to be baptised by you,” he said, “and you come to me?”
“Let it be so for now,” said Jesus. “It is right for us to do this.” So John baptised him in the river.
As Jesus came up out of the water, the heavens opened, and he saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove and resting on him.
And a voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
wonder: I wonder what the water felt like.
I wonder how it felt for Jesus to hear that he was loved.
I wonder if you know that God loves you too.
prayer: Thank you, God, that you call Jesus your beloved Son, and that you love me as your child. Amen.

title: The net full of fish
text: One morning Jesus was by the lake of Galilee, and so many people crowded round to hear him that he got into a fishing boat that belonged to a man called Simon, and taught them from the water.
When he had finished, he said to Simon, “Go out into the deep water, and let down your nets for a catch.”
“Master,” said Simon, “we worked hard all night and caught nothing. But because you say so, I'll let down the nets.”

They rowed out and let down the nets, and suddenly the nets were full of fish: so many fish that the nets began to break! They called their friends James and John in the other boat to help, and they filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
Simon fell at Jesus's knees. “Go away from me, Lord,” he said. “I'm not good enough.”
But Jesus said, “Don't be afraid. From now on you will catch people.” So they brought their boats to land, left everything, and followed him.
wonder: I wonder how Simon felt after a whole night of catching nothing.
I wonder why he did what Jesus said anyway.
I wonder what it means to follow Jesus.
prayer: Dear Jesus, when I am tired and things go wrong, help me try again with you. I want to follow you. Amen.

title: The wedding party
text: There was a wedding in the village of Cana, and Jesus, his mother Mary and his friends were all invited. There was music and food and dancing, and everyone was happy.
But in the middle of the party, the wine ran out! That would be very embarrassing for the family.
Mary went to Jesus. “They have no wine,” she said. Then she said to the servants, “Whatever he tells you, do it.”
Nearby stood six big stone water jars, each one big enough to hold more than a bath of water. “Fill the jars with water,” said Jesus. So the servants filled them right up to the brim.

“Now pour some out and take it to the man in charge of the feast,” said Jesus. The man tasted it, and it had become wine! He didn't know where it came from. He called the bridegroom and said, “Everyone serves the best wine first. But you have kept the best until now!”
This was the first of the signs Jesus did, and it showed his glory. And his friends believed in him.
wonder: I wonder what the servants thought as they carried the water.
I wonder why Jesus's first sign was at a party.
I wonder what makes you feel full of joy.
prayer: Thank you, Jesus, for happy days and parties and good things. Thank you for keeping the best till last. Amen.

title: Through the roof
text: Jesus came home to the town of Capernaum, and news spread fast. So many people came to the house to hear him that there was no room left, not even outside the door.
Then four friends arrived, carrying a man on a mat. He couldn't walk, and they wanted Jesus to make him well. But they couldn't get anywhere near him through the crowd.
So what did they do? They climbed up onto the flat roof, dug a hole right through it, and let their friend down on his mat, right in front of Jesus!
Jesus saw how much faith they had. He said to the man, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”

Some teachers there grumbled inside, “Only God can forgive sins!” Jesus knew what they were thinking. “So that you may know that I have authority to forgive,” he said, and he turned to the man, “get up, take up your mat, and go home.”
And the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of everyone! They were all amazed, and praised God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
wonder: I wonder what the people in the house thought when bits of roof started falling.
I wonder what it's like to have friends like that.
I wonder who you could carry to Jesus in your prayers.
prayer: Dear Jesus, thank you for good friends. Tonight I bring you someone who needs help: ____. Amen.

title: Jesus calms the storm
text: One evening, after a long day of teaching, Jesus said to his friends, “Let's go across to the other side of the lake.” So they got into the boat and set off.
Jesus was tired. He lay down in the back of the boat with his head on a cushion, and fell fast asleep.
Then a great storm blew up. The wind howled, and the waves crashed over the side, and the boat began to fill with water.
His friends were terrified. They woke him up: “Teacher, don't you care that we're going to drown?”
Jesus got up. He spoke to the wind and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” And the wind stopped, and there was a great calm.
Jesus said to them, “Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?” And they whispered to each other, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
wonder: I wonder how Jesus could sleep in a storm.
I wonder what the sudden quiet sounded like.
I wonder what feels stormy to you, that you could give to Jesus tonight.
prayer: Jesus, when I am afraid, say to my heart, “Peace, be still.” Amen.

title: The lost sheep
text: Lots of people came to listen to Jesus, including some who were known for doing bad things. Some religious leaders grumbled, “This man welcomes sinners, and even eats with them!”
So Jesus told them a story.
“Imagine you have a hundred sheep, and one of them gets lost. Won't you leave the ninety-nine safe in the field and go looking for the one that is lost, until you find it?”

“And when you find it, you lift it onto your shoulders, full of joy, and carry it home. Then you call your friends and neighbours together and say, ‘Celebrate with me! I've found my sheep that was lost!’”
“In the same way,” said Jesus, “there is more joy in heaven over one person who turns back to God than over ninety-nine who don't think they need to.”
Every single one matters to God. Even the smallest, even the one who wandered off. Especially that one.
wonder: I wonder how the little sheep felt when it was lost.
I wonder how it felt to be carried home on the shepherd's shoulders.
I wonder if you have ever felt lost, and been found.
prayer: Thank you, Jesus, Good Shepherd, that you come looking for me. Carry me home. Amen.

title: The son who came home
text: Jesus told another story. “There was a man who had two sons. The younger one said, ‘Father, give me my share of your money now.’ So the father gave it to him.
“The son went far away and spent it all on wild living. Then a famine came, and he had nothing left. He took a job looking after pigs, and he was so hungry he wanted to eat the pigs' food.

“At last he came to his senses. ‘My father's servants have more than enough to eat, and here I am starving! I'll go home and say, “Father, I have done wrong. I don't deserve to be your son. Let me be one of your servants.”’
“So he set off home. But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him, and his heart filled with love. He ran to his son, threw his arms around him and kissed him.

“The son began, ‘Father, I have done wrong…’ But the father called to the servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him, a ring for his finger and shoes for his feet. Let's have a feast! For my son was lost, and is found!’

“The older brother was cross that his father was so generous. But the father said, ‘My son, you are always with me, and all I have is yours. But we had to celebrate. Your brother was lost, and now he is found.’”
wonder: I wonder what the son was thinking all the long way home.
I wonder why the father ran.
I wonder how the older brother could join the party.
prayer: Thank you, God, that you run to meet me when I come back to you. Help me forgive others like that too. Amen.

title: Let the children come
text: Wherever Jesus went, people brought him their children, so that he would touch them and bless them.
But Jesus's friends told the parents off. “Go away,” they said. “Jesus is far too busy and important for children.”
When Jesus saw this, he was not pleased with his friends at all.
“Let the little children come to me,” he said. “Don't stop them! For God's kingdom belongs to people like these.”
“I tell you the truth: whoever doesn't receive God's kingdom like a little child will never enter it.”
Then Jesus took the children in his arms, put his hands on them, and blessed them.
wonder: I wonder what it felt like to be held by Jesus.
I wonder what children know about God that grown-ups forget.
I wonder what you would say to Jesus if you could sit on his lap.
prayer: Thank you, Jesus, that you always have time for children. I'm coming to you now. Bless me tonight. Amen.

title: The last supper
text: It was the feast of Passover, when God's people remember how God set them free from Egypt. Jesus gathered his twelve friends in an upstairs room to eat the special meal together.
During supper, Jesus did something surprising. He got up, tied a towel round his waist, poured water into a bowl, and began to wash his friends' dusty feet. That was a servant's job!

Peter said, “Lord, you'll never wash my feet!” But Jesus said, “Unless I wash you, you have no part with me.” When he had finished, he said, “I have given you an example. Do for each other what I have done for you.”
Then Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them. “This is my body, which is given for you,” he said. “Do this to remember me.”
After supper he took the cup of wine. “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.”
Jesus knew that hard days were coming. But he spent his last evening with his friends serving them, sharing bread with them, and loving them to the end.
wonder: I wonder how it felt to have Jesus wash your feet.
I wonder why Jesus wanted to be remembered with bread.
I wonder how you could serve someone in our family tomorrow.
prayer: Dear Jesus, thank you for loving your friends to the end. Help me serve others the way you did. Amen.

title: Easter morning
text: Jesus had died on a cross on Friday, and his friends had laid his body in a tomb cut into the rock, with a big stone across the door. They were heartbroken.

Very early on Sunday morning, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb. The stone had been rolled away! She ran to tell Peter and John, and they ran to see. The tomb was empty, with only the burial cloths lying there.
Peter and John went home, but Mary stayed outside the tomb, crying.
Then she turned round and saw a man standing there. She thought he was the gardener. “Sir,” she said, “if you have taken him away, tell me where he is.”
The man said one word: “Mary.” And she knew that voice! It was Jesus, alive! “Teacher!” she cried.
Jesus sent her to tell the others. So Mary ran to his friends with the best news in the world: “I have seen the Lord!”
wonder: I wonder how Mary felt when she heard Jesus say her name.
I wonder why the first person to see Jesus alive was someone who was crying.
I wonder who you would run to tell.
prayer: Jesus, you are alive! Thank you that you know my name, and that love is stronger than death. Alleluia! Amen.

title: The road to Emmaus
text: On that same Easter Sunday, two of Jesus's friends were walking sadly home to a village called Emmaus. They were talking about everything that had happened.
A stranger came and walked along with them. It was Jesus, but somehow they didn't recognise him.

“What are you talking about?” he asked. They stood still, looking sad. “Haven't you heard? Jesus, who we hoped would save Israel, was killed. And this morning some women said his tomb is empty and that angels said he was alive!”
Then the stranger explained to them, all the way along the road, everything the Scriptures said about the Messiah. As he talked, their hearts felt warm inside.

When they reached the village, it was getting dark. “Stay with us,” they said. So he went in to eat with them. He took the bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them, and suddenly their eyes were opened. It was Jesus! And then he vanished.
They didn't wait till morning. They ran all the way back to Jerusalem in the dark to tell the others: “The Lord is risen! We knew him when he broke the bread!”
wonder: I wonder why they didn't recognise Jesus at first.
I wonder what made their hearts feel warm.
I wonder where Jesus might be walking with us, without us noticing.
prayer: Stay with us, Lord Jesus, for it is evening and the day is almost over. Amen.
